Equality Objectives
E-ACT is committed to ensuring equality of opportunity in line with the Equality Act 2010. E-ACT seeks to reduce disadvantages, discrimination and inequalities of opportunity, and promote diversity in terms of its students, workforce and the communities it serves. Unlawful discrimination and harassment of any member of the academy community is expressly prohibited, and E-ACT is committed to protecting all pupils/students/staff and prospective staff from unlawful discrimination and harassment.
We are committed to:
The need to eliminate discrimination, harassment and victimisation advancing equality of opportunity between different groups fostering good relations between different groups
The Crest is an inclusive school, where we focus on the well-being and progress of every student and where all members of our community are of equal worth.
We believe that the Equality Act provides a framework to support our commitment to valuing diversity, tackling discrimination, promoting equality and fostering good relationships between people. It also ensures that we continue to tackle issues of disadvantage and underachievement of different groups.
Our approach to equality is based on the following key principles:
1. All learners are of equal value.
2. We recognise and respect difference.
3. We foster positive attitudes and relationships and a shared sense of cohesion and belonging.
4. We observe good equalities practice in staff recruitment, retention and development.
5. We aim to reduce and remove inequalities and barriers that already exist.
6. We have the highest expectations of our children. We ensure that our pupils are exposed to and taught about all protected characteristics through our curriculum.
Date of Review: October 2023
Date of Next Review: October 2026

SPIRIT
Our SPIRIT Values
At E-ACT Crest Academy, our values are at the heart of who we are. They shape our culture, guide our decisions and establish the expectations we have for every member of our Academy community.
Together, our six values form SPIRIT:
S – SuccessP – PerseveranceI – IntegrityR – ResilienceI – IndependenceT – Thoughtfulness
SPIRIT is much more than an acronym. It represents the qualities and character we want every Crest student to develop throughout their journey with us.
Our values can be seen in everything we do: in our classrooms, our approach to learning, our behaviour and routines, the relationships we build, the way we treat one another and the contribution we make to our wider community.
We want our students not only to achieve excellent academic outcomes, but also to leave Crest as confident, responsible and thoughtful young people, equipped with the character and determination to succeed in the next stage of their lives.
Success
We aim high and strive to achieve our very best.
Success is at the heart of our Academy motto: Success in Everything We Do. We encourage every student to be ambitious for themselves and to recognise that success comes in many forms.
In the classroom, success means working hard, making progress and taking pride in the quality of our work. Across Academy life, it means setting high standards, embracing opportunities and continually seeking to improve.
We celebrate achievement while always asking: What can I do next to become even better?
Perseverance
We keep going, even when things become difficult.
Learning is not always easy, and success rarely happens without challenge. We teach our students to persevere, remain focused and continue trying when they encounter something difficult.
Students are encouraged to seek help, respond positively to feedback and understand that effort, practice and determination are essential parts of improvement.
At Crest, we do not give up when something is difficult. We keep going, keep learning and keep improving.
Integrity
We do the right thing, even when nobody is watching.
Integrity is fundamental to our culture and ethos. We expect our students to be honest, respectful and responsible for their choices.
This means following Academy expectations, treating others with dignity, looking after our community and having the courage to make the right decision.
We want students to understand that character is demonstrated not simply by what we say, but by the choices we make every day.
Resilience
We learn from setbacks and come back stronger.
Every young person will experience challenges, mistakes and setbacks. What matters is how we respond to them.
At Crest, we teach students that making a mistake does not define them. We encourage them to reflect, learn, reset and try again.
Whether overcoming a difficult piece of learning, responding to feedback or recovering from a poor choice, resilience means developing the confidence and strength to move forward positively.
Independence
We take responsibility for our learning, our choices and our future.
Our students are supported to become increasingly independent as they progress through the Academy.
This starts with everyday habits: arriving on time, being properly equipped, completing independent learning, reading regularly, following routines and taking responsibility for missed learning.
It also means developing the confidence to think critically, solve problems, make informed decisions and take ownership of personal development.
Our ambition is for every student to leave Crest prepared to take responsibility for the future they want to create.
Thoughtfulness
We consider others and think about the impact of our words and actions.
Crest is a diverse community, and we want every student to feel safe, respected and that they belong.
Thoughtfulness means showing kindness, listening to others, respecting difference and considering how our behaviour affects the people around us.
It means celebrating the success of others, helping someone who needs support and contributing positively to our Academy and wider community.
Through thoughtfulness, we develop a culture where everyone is valued and everyone can thrive.
Success in Everything We Do!
Our SPIRIT values are not confined to assemblies, posters or displays. They are lived every day.
In learning, SPIRIT means aiming for success, persevering through challenge, working independently and responding resiliently when things go wrong.
In behaviour, it means demonstrating integrity, taking responsibility for our choices and showing thoughtfulness towards others.
In our culture and ethos, it means maintaining high expectations while creating a community built upon respect, belonging, ambition and kindness.
In character development, it means helping students understand who they are, what they stand for and the type of person they want to become.
Ultimately, education at Crest is about more than qualifications. We have a responsibility to prepare young people for life beyond the Academy. Through our SPIRIT values, we seek to develop students who are ambitious, determined, honest, resilient, independent and thoughtful.
These values unite our Academy community and underpin our commitment to achieving Success in Everything We Do.

Our ethos and values
At The Crest Academy, we believe that our school should take its rightful place at the heart of the community — as a centre of excellence, a place of inspiration, and the first-choice school for families in Brent.
Our mission is simple yet powerful:We are committed to transforming the life chances of every student by providing a world-class education that equips them with the knowledge, character, and confidence to succeed in further education, employment, and life.
“Success in Everything we do”
We believe that every student can achieve excellence when they are inspired, nurtured, and challenged to be their best selves. We develop young people who are leaders of their own learning, who act with integrity, show resilience in the face of challenge, and contribute positively to society.
Everything we do at The Crest Academy is underpinned by our core SPIRIT values:
Success – We set ambitious goals and strive for excellence in all that we do.
Perseverance – We show determination and resilience to overcome challenges.
Integrity – We are honest, respectful, and do the right thing, even when no one is watching.
Resilience – We bounce back from setbacks and learn from every experience.
Independence – We take responsibility for our actions, learning, and future.
Thoughtfulness – We show empathy, kindness, and care towards others.
We are a school that values inclusion, celebrates diversity, and champions equity. At Crest, every young person is known, valued, and empowered to thrive. Our aim is not just to educate, but to inspire the leaders of tomorrow — young people who will leave us ready to make a positive impact on their community, their city, and the wider world.

Welcome from the Head of Sixth Form
Dear Parents and Carers,
Welcome to the Sixth Form at The E-ACT Crest Academy — a vibrant, ambitious, and inclusive community where students are empowered to thrive academically, socially, and personally.
At Crest, we offer a broad and balanced curriculum designed to meet the diverse aspirations of our students. Whether your goals lie in university study, vocational pathways, or professional careers, our curriculum provides the depth and flexibility to support your journey. From A Levels to vocational qualifications, our subjects are taught by passionate, expert staff who are committed to helping every student achieve their full potential.
But our offer goes far beyond the classroom.
We are proud to be home to one of the most dynamic basketball programmes in London. Our elite training and competitive fixtures are complemented by a strong academic foundation, creating a unique dual pathway for talented athletes. Many of our students have gone on to secure scholarships to study in the United States, combining high-level sport with world-class education. If you’re passionate about basketball and driven to succeed, Crest is the place to be.
Our Sixth Form is more than just a stepping stone — it’s a launchpad. With tailored support, leadership opportunities, enrichment activities, and a culture of high expectations, we prepare our students not only for exams, but for life beyond school.
We invite you to explore what makes Crest Sixth Form exceptional. Join us, and become part of a community that believes in your potential and invests in your future.
Mr Aaron Newell Assistant Headteacher/Head of Sixth Form The E-ACT Crest Academy

Meet our Headteacher
A very warm welcome to E-ACT Crest Academy.
I am thrilled to introduce myself as the Headteacher of E-Act Crest Academy. It is with great honour and enthusiasm that I take on this role, as I feel privileged to lead the fantastic staff and students, with a focus not only on academic achievement but also the holistic development of each student.
At E-Act Crest Academy, we believe that each child is a unique individual. We will therefore strive to provide them with education that equips them with the skills and knowledge they need to succeed in an ever-changing world. We will ensure that your child will be able to come to the academy every day into a stimulating, calm, purposeful and safe learning environment, where they will thrive, be independent and resilient.
I firmly believe in the core values: SPIRIT (Success, Perseverance, Integrity, Resilience, Independence and Thoughtfulness) which will be at the heart of everything that we do at our school. Our motto, ‘Success in Everything We Do’ is embedded throughout our academy along with the E-Act values, ‘think big’, ‘show team spirit’ and ‘do the right thing’.
Here at E-Act Crest, we believe in high expectations for ourselves as teachers and for your child. We strive to give every child a broad, balanced, and enjoyable curriculum for them to achieve their potential and experience learning, both inside and outside of the classroom, in a range of creative ways, as we have a commitment to inclusive teaching.
We are committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of our children as they develop as happy, confident, and valued individuals. I believe that strong partnerships with parents and the wider community are vital to the success of our school. Your support, involvement, and feedback are highly valued, so I strongly recommend open communication between home and school.
I am excited about the journey ahead and the possibilities it holds for your child at this school, as together we can create an inclusive and supportive community where every individual is valued and respected.
We hope that you take the time to look through our website and school prospectus.
Please make an appointment to come and have a look around the academy where you will be most welcomed.
Ms Rosewell Headteacher

Our curriculum
The curriculum and its delivery are the very foundation of what a school offers and the reason it exists. The following policy sets out the main principles that shapes the curriculum at E-Act Crest Academy and consequently its intent, implementation and how its impact will be measured and evaluated.
The principles of E-ACT Crest Academy are firstly shaped by the trust, and then by the school’s values, mission and vision as set out below:
‘Opening minds, opening doors.
We will open minds and open doors for our pupils, our staff and our communities by:
Having uncompromising aspirations for all.
Having the best people and investing in them.
Understanding, celebrating and working with our communities.’
Our Vision for the curriculum at E-ACT Crest Academy is driven by our belief in the power that a great curriculum has to transform lives, not just by securing excellent qualifications but by developing every young person socially, spiritually, morally, emotionally and culturally, allowing them to mature into young adults fully equipped to realise their dreams and ambitions. To achieve this, our mission is to provide every student with the essential knowledge, skills and cultural capital to thrive both in their education and in modern society.
The intent of our curriculum is to provide a solid foundation across a wide range of disciplines through our comprehensive and ambitious 3 year Key Stage 3 programme, which allows us to be ambitious for Key Stage 4, where all students continue to study an academic curriculum, taking one the humanities subjects with as many as possible also studying a language to complete the Ebacc qualification. This will maximise the number of students equipped to progress to higher education. Further, our ambition at KS5 is demonstrated by our subject offering that gives the students opportunities to pursue academic and vocational pathways at the
Our curriculum is primarily knowledge-based and is carefully planned by each Curriculum Director or Subject Lead to ensure students learn the knowledge and key concepts for that discipline, while also developing the skills they need to be successful. Teachers plan lessons that inspire students to enjoy learning, want to know more, encourage them to think and work independently, in turn preparing them for the next steps in their education.
Our curriculum is underpinned by a commitment to equality of opportunity and complies with the Equality Act (2010) and Special Educational Needs Code of practice (2014). We strive to ensure that all students are able to succeed no matter what their starting point is. Some will require specialist teaching to help develop the basics that were not formed appropriately in Key Stage 1 and 2 through formal teaching of Phonics. For others this will be the development of subject specific language and knowledge through specialist teachers. All teachers know their classes and the individuals in them and so ensure that lessons are personalised and specific needs are catered for.
The personal development curriculum meets all statutory requirements, including health, staying safe, and RSE, as well as citizenship and safeguarding. The personal development curriculum is delivered through the tutor time programme and a dedicated session of curriculum time for KS3. Students are taught how to be responsible global citizens who engage in British values live happy and healthy lives and know how to achieve their life goals and secure their economic wellbeing.
Organisation – Key Stage 3
At Key Stage 3, we deliver the National Curriculum. This provides all students with a firm foundation across a wide range of disciplines and ensures that students have a secure grounding in all curriculum subjects before selecting their options. We have carefully balanced the curriculum provision so that all students make excellent progress in the core subjects whilst having sufficient time to develop their talents in the arts, humanities and languages. This ensures that all students have the opportunity to progress to the English Baccalaureate qualification at Key Stage 4.
In Years 7-9 students are taught in mixed ability classes. We believe that mixed ability provides more benefit for the majority of our students. This enables teachers to organise groups around a range of criteria such as behaviour, a balance of gender, and balance of academic ability. We believe children learn from each other; therefore, the brightest students learn from ‘teaching’ and sharing their knowledge with others and less academic students learn from their peers to support the learning gained from their teachers.

Organisation – Key Stage 4
The intention of the KS4 curriculum is to develop a deep understanding of the core curriculum and the subjects of personal interest to each student which in turn will prepare students for external examinations. Students continue with their core subjects in Key Stage 4 and select 3 options.
The KS4 Curriculum model September 2025
The KS4 Curriculum model September 2025 All students study the core subjects of Maths, English and Science. Each of these follows a 5-lessons per week programme. Students then have 3 options choices. These include subjects such as; Spanish, History, Geography, Art, IT, Business Studies, Health and Social Care, Sport, and Arabic. This gives the students a wide choice in line with their interests and aspirations. Each of these follows a 3-lessons per week programme. All students at KS4 have a Core PE lesson each week.
Citizenship, RE, PSHE,RSE, Personal Development, Careers, Safeguarding
Citizenship, RE, PSHE,RSE, Personal Development, Careers, Safeguarding
Organisation – Key Stage 5
At Key Stage 5 we aim to build on the strong foundations of the Key Stage 4 curriculum by ensuring students study an appropriate curriculum for their future needs and goals. We encourage them to maintain breadth and balance as much as is appropriate in line with their interests.
The curriculum is designed for students who will thrive in an educational environment where the rigours and demands of the different subjects are embraced and taught in a supportive manner without compromising the academic challenges of Sixth Form study.
Whilst the majority of subjects on offer are A Level qualifications, some subjects follow a vocational route, in order to support students who have specific vocational paths in mind or who have a preferred learning style different to that required for the A Level qualifications.
Whereas the A Levels are assessed predominantly through external examinations, the Vocational courses will have a greater percentage of coursework involved. A student can choose to follow either route or a combination of both. Whichever pathway a student follows, the aim is to build upon the foundation, knowledge and skills gained throughout their KS3 and KS4 study.
At the point of enrolment, students are guided in their course choices so that they follow a cohesive and coherent programme of study where the content and skills of the individual subjects complement each other, as well as furnishing students with a depth of cultural, social and intellectual ideas.
Students are given the opportunity to choose a minimum of three and can study a maximum of four.
The subjects that students can choose from are listed below:
GCSE English Language
BTEC Business and Double Business
BTEC Applied Science, double, and triple Applied Science
A-level Further Maths
BTEC Health and Social Care
Curriculum Planning and Review
The implementation of our curriculum across the academy is illustrated below. It starts out with the planning of long- and medium-term plans and lesson materials and their delivery in the classroom. Their success is then tested using a range of assessment methods. At the same time, senior leasers assure the quality of delivery and impact through lesson drop-ins, book scrutiny and student voice interviews. This then informs Subject Directors to inform their planning and help identify training and development needs.

Personal Development
Personal Development at Crest Academy
At Crest, our intent is to embed the ethos of ‘success in everything we do’ across all aspects of school life. Through our Personal Development programme, we ensure that every student is supported to become a well-rounded, confident, compassionate and capable individual who achieves success and makes meaningful contributions to society.
Our personal development approach is driven by six core values:
· Success: We raise ambition and promote a growth mindset, enabling all students to recognise their achievements and develop the skills to excel in all aspects of life.
· Perseverance: We support all students to develop determination and a strong sense of purpose, helping them overcome personal and academic challenges.
· Integrity: We cultivate a culture of respect and ethical behaviour, encouraging all students to act with honesty and integrity in all decisions and interactions.
· Resilience: We equip all students with the confidence and positivity needed to adapt to life’s challenges and maintain long-term wellbeing.
· Independence: We empower all students to become self-reliant, critical thinkers who take ownership of their learning and personal growth.
· Thoughtfulness: We encourage all students to consider their impact on others and their community, fostering kindness, inclusion, and social responsibility.
This intent underpins every element of our curriculum, enrichment offer, careers programme, and wellbeing provision, ensuring a coherent and ambitious Personal Development journey for all students.

Governance Information
E-ACT is a multi-academy trust responsible for the governance and strategic oversight of all E-ACT academies.
The Board of Trustees is accountable for the performance of the Trust and its academies. Trustees set the strategic direction of E-ACT, oversee educational and financial performance, and ensure compliance with statutory and regulatory requirements.
Through its governance structure, E-ACT provides effective oversight while empowering academy leaders to deliver excellent outcomes for pupils.
Governance at E-ACT
OUR GOVERNANCE STRUCTURE
Members: Members act as the guardians of E-ACT’s charitable purpose. They ensure the Trust remains true to its mission and values and are responsible for appointing trustees and approving significant constitutional changes.
Board of Trustees: The Board of Trustees oversees the strategic direction and performance of the Trust. Trustees ensure E-ACT meets its legal obligations, uses public funds responsibly and delivers high-quality education across all academies. They hold the CEO and Executive Leadership Team to account for educational and financial performance.
Chief Executive Officer (CEO) and National Leadership Team: The CEO leads the Trust, supported by the National Leadership Team. Together, they implement the Trust’s strategy, oversee educational, financial and operational performance, and ensure academies receive the support they need to succeed.
Academy Headteachers: Headteachers lead their academies on a day-to-day basis, ensuring high standards of education, safeguarding, behaviour and pupil wellbeing. They work closely with the National Leadership Team to deliver strong outcomes for pupils.
Academy Ambassadors: Academy Ambassadors provide local insight, support and constructive challenge. They help strengthen engagement between the academy, its community and the Trust, but do not hold delegated governance responsibilities.

Academy Ambassadors
Every E-ACT academy is supported by an Academy Ambassador Group. Ambassador Groups connect academies with their local communities, bringing valuable insight, experience and perspective to support the success of the academy and enrich Trust-wide governance.
E-ACT has established an Ambassador Group in every academy because local voice is essential. Ambassador Groups help ensure that each academy remains connected to its community and that the views of parents, pupils and local stakeholders help inform the Trust’s understanding of academy life.
Ambassador Groups are not governance bodies and do not hold delegated decision-making powers. Their role is to strengthen the partnership between the academy, its community and E-ACT through three key pillars:
Membership
Each Academy Ambassador Group includes the Headteacher and two Parent Ambassadors elected in accordance with E-ACT’s Articles of Association.
Groups may also include individuals from the local community who can contribute their skills, experience, networks and local knowledge to support the academy and its pupils. Membership is designed to reflect the diversity and needs of the academy community while bringing together a broad range of perspectives.

Ambassador Charter
All Academy Ambassadors are expected to uphold the values of E-ACT and work in accordance with the Ambassador Group Charter, which sets out the commitments and expectations of Ambassadors, academies, the Trust and the Board of Trustees.
